prompt: You have 20,000 approved support replies in your brand voice, and long style prompts still give inconsistent tone.
tells: long style prompts still give inconsistent tone
why: Lots of examples of a consistent style that prompting can't pin down: train it in.
trap: Prompting is the first lever, but here it's already been pushed and fallen short.

prompt: A large model classifies tickets well, but at 50 million tickets a month it's too slow and expensive. You have its labels for 200,000 tickets.
why: Distill: fine-tune a small model on the big model's labels for a narrow, high-volume task.
trap: Routing still sends many tickets to the big model; a narrow task can be handed entirely to a tuned small one.

prompt: Radiology reports must follow a rigid house format and shorthand. You have 50,000 past reports, and few-shot prompts fill the context and still drift.
tells: few-shot prompts fill the context and still drift
why: A specialized writing style with abundant examples is what fine-tuning is good at.
trap: Structured output fixes field shape, not clinical shorthand and phrasing inside the text.

prompt: An autocomplete feature needs answers in under 100 ms, which only a small model can hit, but the small model's quality on your task is poor. You have plenty of labeled examples.
tells: only a small model can hit
small model's quality on your task is poor
why: Train the small model on your task so it's both fast and good enough.
trap: Streaming improves perceived latency for long answers; autocomplete needs the whole answer fast.

prompt: A frontier model writes great product titles but costs too much at 5 million calls a day. You have 100,000 of its best outputs saved.
tells: costs too much at 5 million calls a day
why: Distill: fine-tune a smaller model on the large model's outputs to match quality at lower cost.
trap: Routing helps only if some calls are easy; here every call needs the same skill.

prompt: A game studio wants every NPC line in a very specific dialect that prompting can't reliably hold. They have 30,000 written lines.
why: Style and voice are what fine-tuning learns best from many examples.
trap: RAG supplies facts, not a way of speaking.

prompt: Your prompt has grown to 6,000 tokens of instructions and examples, and you send it on every one of 2 million daily calls.
why: Fine-tuning moves those instructions into the weights, cutting per-call tokens and cost.
trap: Prompt caching can also help; but when the behavior is stable, training it in removes the prompt entirely.

prompt: A small on-device model must turn spoken commands into one of 40 app actions. Prompting gets 70% right, and you have 25,000 labeled command transcripts.
why: With plenty of labeled examples and a model too small to follow long prompts, fine-tuning teaches the mapping directly.
trap: Structured output fixes the format, not which action the model picks.
